T: Lift the hammer. Then lift a fork.
D: Tony builds a peacekeeping AI that decides humanity is the problem.
P: Serve the snacks when everyone takes a turn trying to lift Thor's hammer at the party.
S: the party at the tower where everyone tries to lift the hammer

Crisp garlic crostini topped with paper-thin seared beef, rocket, shaved parmesan, capers and a drizzle of lemon olive oil. Season a 400g eye fillet, sear hard on all sides for 3 minutes, then wrap tightly in cling film and freeze for 1 hour. Slice a baguette into 20 thin rounds, brush with olive oil and bake at 180C for 10 minutes, then rub with garlic. Slice the beef wafer thin. Top each crostini with rocket and beef, then shaved parmesan from 60g, a few capers, lemon juice and olive oil.
Double-fried crispy wings in a sticky gochujang, honey and garlic glaze
Chicken wings fried twice until crackly, tossed in a sticky sauce of gochujang, honey, garlic and soy, with sesame seeds.
Cheddar potato dumplings boiled then fried with onions, served with sour cream
Potato and cheese dumplings boiled, then fried in butter with onion until golden, served with sour cream.
M: Two lemon thyme roast chickens with potatoes, carrots and pan gravy
Whole chickens roasted with lemon and thyme, with roast potatoes, carrots and a big bowl of gravy on the farmhouse table.
Johannesburg boerewors with pap and relish

Coriander-spiced beef sausage coils grilled over coals, with buttery maize meal pap and a warm tomato and onion relish. Grill 1kg thick beef sausages over medium coals for 15 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. For the relish, soften 2 sliced onions in oil, add 1 tsp ground coriander, 1 tsp curry powder, 4 chopped tomatoes and 1 tbsp sugar, and simmer 15 minutes. Bring 1L salted water to the boil, whisk in 250g fine polenta and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes, then beat in 40g butter.
W: Meringue topped with whipped cream, strawberries and blueberries
Meringue baked at 120C for 90 minutes, cooled in the oven, topped with cream and berries, served on a raised cake stand.
K: Mead with honey, cinnamon and clove syrup, lemon and ginger beer over ice

Honey mead stirred with lemon, a cinnamon and clove honey syrup and ginger beer, served over ice with orange slices. Warm 3 tbsp honey with 3 tbsp water, 1 cinnamon stick and 3 cloves until the honey melts, then cool and strain. In a jug, mix 500ml chilled mead, the honey syrup and the juice of 1 lemon. Add plenty of ice and top with 500ml ginger beer. Pour into 4 glasses with orange slices. For a booze-free jug, use apple juice in place of the mead.

note.text: Come to the farm. Laura cooks, the kids run wild, and nobody is trying to end the world.

winks: Everyone trying to lift the hammer

steps.text: Pat the wings very dry.
Fry at 160C in batches until cooked, then rest on a rack.
Fry again at 190C until crackly and golden.
Warm the gochujang with the honey, garlic and soy until glossy.
Toss the wings through the glaze and scatter with sesame seeds.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day, uncooked and chilled

steps.text: Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with the cheddar and cool.
Fill the wrappers with the potato mixture and pinch closed.
Boil in batches until they float, then drain.
Fry in butter with the onion until golden on both sides.
Serve with sour cream.
Rub the chickens with lemon, thyme, oil and salt and set in a large roasting tray with the potatoes and carrots.
Roast at 200C until the chicken is golden and cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Rest the chickens on a board.
Make gravy in the tray with the flour, juices and stock.
Carve and serve at a big farmhouse table.

dishes.make_ahead: Meringue up to 1 day, keep airtight; top just before serving

steps.text: Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks.
Add the sugar a spoon at a time until thick and glossy.
Shape into a round on a lined tray.
Bake at 120C, then switch the oven off and cool the meringue inside.
Whip the cream, spread over the meringue and top with the berries.

dishes.make_ahead: Syrup up to 3 days, keep chilled

steps.text: Warm the honey with the water, cinnamon and cloves until the honey melts.
Cool and strain the syrup.
In a jug, mix the mead, honey syrup and lemon juice.
Add plenty of ice, top with ginger beer and pour into glasses with orange slices.

s.note: Double-fried crispy wings in a sticky gochujang, honey and garlic glaze
s.how: Fry 1kg chicken wings at 160C for 10 minutes, rest, then fry again at 190C until crackly. Warm 3 tbsp gochujang with 3 tbsp honey, crushed garlic and a splash of soy until glossy. Toss the wings through and scatter with sesame seeds.

s.note: Cheddar potato dumplings boiled then fried with onions, served with sour cream
s.how: Boil and mash 600g potatoes with 150g grated cheddar. Fill dumpling wrappers and pinch closed. Boil for 3 minutes until they float, drain, then fry in butter with sliced onion until golden on both sides. Serve with sour cream.

m.note: Two lemon thyme roast chickens with potatoes, carrots and pan gravy
m.how: Rub 2 whole chickens with lemon, thyme, oil and salt. Roast at 200C for 75 minutes with 1.5kg potatoes and 6 carrots in the tray. Make gravy from the juices and chicken stock. Serve at a big farmhouse table with room for everyone.

w.note: Meringue topped with whipped cream, strawberries and blueberries
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, strawberries and blueberries and lift onto a tall stand.

d.note: Mead with honey, cinnamon and clove syrup, lemon and ginger beer over ice
d.how: Warm 3 tbsp honey with 3 tbsp water, 1 cinnamon stick and 3 cloves until the honey melts, then cool and strain. In a jug, mix 500ml chilled mead, the honey syrup and the juice of 1 lemon. Add plenty of ice and top with 500ml ginger beer. Pour into 4 glasses with orange slices. For a booze-free jug, use apple juice in place of the mead.
